contexts.title: Biodiversity
contexts.definition: What lives where, as Darwin Core and the biodiversity networks (GBIF, iNaturalist) describe it: taxa and their names, records of an organism at a place and time, and the status a taxon holds in a region (native, introduced, invasive, prohibited).

concepts.definition: A named group of organisms at a rank in the tree of life (species, genus, family), as one naming authority records it: its scientific name and authorship, rank, common name and the identifier that authority gives it. Authorities disagree on names, so one plant can carry a different name and identifier in each.
concepts.coRefersRationale: Field Guide Species is a stewardship group's identification card about a taxon, not the taxon itself; it points at one through taxonId.

fields.name: taxonId
fields.description: The authority's identifier (iNaturalist taxon id, GBIF taxonKey, USDA symbol)

fields.name: authority
fields.description: Which naming authority the record and id come from

fields.name: acceptedTaxon
fields.description: For a synonym, the name the authority accepts instead

sourceAttribution.sourceNotes: Fields from Darwin Core taxon terms, the iNaturalist taxa API, GBIF and USDA PLANTS; from the environmental stewardship round, 2026-10-29.

concepts.definition: A record that an organism of a taxon was (or was looked for and not) at a place at a time: who recorded it, how (human observation, machine, specimen), how sure the identification is, how precise the location is, and whether it was wild or planted.
concepts.coRefersRationale: Environmental Monitoring Observation is a measured value at a fixed station; an occurrence records an organism.

fields.name: coordinatesObscured
fields.description: True when the publisher blurred the location (threatened species, observer's choice)

sourceAttribution.sourceNotes: Fields from Darwin Core occurrence terms, the GBIF occurrence API and the iNaturalist observations API; 2026-10-29.

concepts.definition: The standing a naming or regulating authority gives a taxon in a region: native, introduced, invasive, potentially invasive or prohibited, with any legal effect and its date, the list it comes from, and the name the list uses for the taxon.
concepts.coRefersRationale: Species Watchlist Entry is one site's choice to watch a species; this is an authority's statement about a region.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.description: The name as the list writes it; may be a synonym of another authority's name

fields.name: region
fields.description: ISO 3166-2 code or the authority's region code (US-CT, CT, L48)

fields.name: legalStatus
fields.description: Any legal effect, e.g. sale and import prohibited by statute, with its effective date

sourceAttribution.importedFrom: Darwin Core Species Distribution extension; GRIIS; state invasive lists
sourceAttribution.sourceNotes: Shaped by the CT Invasive Plant List (CIPWG) and USDA PLANTS NativeStatuses; 2026-10-29.

concepts.definition: A stretch of river, lake or estuary that a state assesses against its water quality standards for a reporting cycle: whether it supports its designated uses (swimming, aquatic life, fish consumption), the causes of any impairment, and whether it is on the impaired-waters list or has a cleanup plan.
concepts.coRefersRationale: Monitoring Site is a sampling station; the assessment unit is the reach whose condition the samples inform.

sourceAttribution.sourceNotes: Fields from EPA's ATTAINS Assessment map service; 2026-10-29.

concepts.definition: An area a government designates for environmental justice purposes (a census block group, tract or municipality) under a stated test such as the share of residents below twice the poverty line, with the year of the designation and the figures it rests on.
concepts.coRefersRationale: City District and census tracts are the geographies; this is a designation over one of them.

fields.name: geoid
fields.description: Census GEOID, or the state's town code for a municipality

fields.name: percentLowIncome
fields.description: Share of residents below 200% of the federal poverty level

sourceAttribution.sourceNotes: Fields from CT DEEP's 2025 EJ block groups and distressed municipalities layers; 2026-10-29.

concepts.definition: The land that drains to one outlet, as a hydrologic unit with a hierarchical code (HUC2 to HUC12), its name and area, and the unit it drains into.
concepts.coRefersRationale: No existing concept describes drainage areas.

fields.name: drainsTo
fields.description: HUC code of the downstream unit

concepts.definition: One organized effort to record the organisms at a place over a set time (a bioblitz, a transect walk, a point count) under a stated protocol, with the effort spent and who took part, so that what was found and what was not can be compared between years and places.
concepts.coRefersRationale: Volunteer Event is a workday; a survey event's records are occurrences, and its protocol and effort make absences meaningful.

fields.name: parentEvent
fields.description: A larger survey this one is part of (a city-wide bioblitz)

fields.name: taxaTargeted
fields.description: Plants, pollinators, birds…: what absences mean

fields.name: recordLicense
fields.description: The license the event's records are shared under (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-NC)

sourceAttribution.sourceNotes: From the Garden BioBlitz case study, 2026-10-29.

sources.title: Darwin Core terms
sources.recordDescription: The shared vocabulary for biodiversity records: occurrences of organisms, taxa, events and locations.

sources.title: iNaturalist observations (API v1)
sources.publisher: iNaturalist (California Academy of Sciences and National Geographic Society)
sources.recordDescription: One observation a person posted of an organism, with photos, the community's identification and its quality grade.
sources.license: Per observation and per photo (license_code); some are all rights reserved
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29: 1,506 research-grade observations within 1 km of the Mill River at Fair Haven. Names follow iNaturalist's taxonomy (Japanese knotweed is Reynoutria japonica, not the CT list's Polygonum cuspidatum): join on taxon ids or synonyms, not names.

queryNotes.defaults: Every quality grade (casual, needs_id, research) and 30 per page.
queryNotes.filters: lat+lng+radius (km), place_id, taxon_id, quality_grade=research, d1/d2 dates; introduced=true or native=true need a place_id.
queryNotes.lifecycle: Identifications change as the community weighs in, and quality_grade with them; re-fetch rather than keep old names.
queryNotes.clients: Read iNaturalist's API recommended practices before bulk use (rate and daily limits); obscured observations blur coordinates by design.

sources.title: iNaturalist taxa (API v1)
sources.publisher: iNaturalist (California Academy of Sciences and National Geographic Society)
sources.recordDescription: One taxon in iNaturalist's taxonomy, with its rank, common name, parent and counts of observations.

sources.title: GBIF occurrence search (API v1)
sources.recordDescription: One occurrence record shared to GBIF by a museum, survey or citizen-science network, in Darwin Core terms.
sources.cost: None: public JSON, no key for search (observed 2026-10-29).
sources.license: Per record (CC0, CC BY or CC BY-NC); cite the dataset
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29: 51,478 occurrences in a small box around the Mill River, including iNaturalist research-grade records (so the two overlap; drop duplicates by occurrenceID). Names are GBIF's backbone: taxonKey joins across datasets.

queryNotes.filters: decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude ranges, taxonKey, year, basisOfRecord, datasetKey, establishmentMeans.
queryNotes.paging: limit up to 300 with offset; search paging stops at 100,000; use the download API beyond that.

sources.title: USDA PLANTS plant profile
sources.recordDescription: One plant in the USDA PLANTS database, with its accepted name, growth habit and native or introduced status by region.
sources.readinessNote: Undocumented JSON behind plants.usda.gov: ?symbol=<USDA symbol>. A synonym's symbol returns the accepted plant: FAJA2 (Fallopia japonica) came back as POCU6, Polygonum cuspidatum. ScientificName carries <i> tags. NativeStatuses lists regions (L48, CAN, AK...), not states.

sources.title: Connecticut Invasive Plant List
sources.publisher: Connecticut Invasive Plants Council / CT Invasive Plant Working Group (UConn)
sources.recordDescription: One plant the Connecticut Invasive Plants Council lists as invasive or potentially invasive, with whether state law prohibits it.
sources.readinessNote: An HTML page (and 2025 PDFs), not data: about 102 entries, 54 marked (P) for potentially invasive. Statute prohibitions can carry a future date (Norway maple: Oct. 2030). Names are the list's own (Polygonum cuspidatum for Japanese knotweed), so match to iNaturalist via synonyms or USDA symbols.

queryNotes.allRecords: One page lists every entry, sorted by botanical name; a second sorts by common name; PDFs are linked from the page.

fields.name: scientificName
fields.description: Before the dash in each entry

fields.name: prohibitedByStatute
fields.description: Yes, No or N/A, sometimes with an effective date

sources.title: EPA ATTAINS assessment units (lines: rivers and streams)
sources.recordDescription: One river or stream reach a state assessed for its water quality report, with use support, impairment causes and listing status.
sources.cost: No key for the map service (observed 2026-10-29); the ATTAINS REST API needs an api.data.gov key.
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29: Connecticut has several Mill Rivers (Hamden, New Canaan/Stamford, Easton/Monroe): filter by assessmentunitidentifier, never by name. Rows can repeat with identical attributes; de-duplicate by assessmentunitidentifier and reportingcycle. Estuary reaches are in the Areas layer (MapServer/2).

queryNotes.filters: where on state, assessmentunitidentifier, reportingcycle, overallstatus.
queryNotes.recordLink: waterbodyreportlink is the state's report page for the unit.

sources.title: CT DEEP Environmental Justice Block Groups 2025
sources.publisher: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
sources.recordDescription: One census block group Connecticut designates as an environmental justice community for 2025, with its share of residents below 200% of the poverty line.
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29: 738 block groups, from 2024 ACS 5-year poverty estimates. GEOID joins census layers; TOWN_NO is the state town code (93 = New Haven). There is one set per year (2021-2025): say which year a grant narrative uses.

sources.title: CT DEEP Environmental Justice Distressed Municipalities 2025
sources.publisher: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
sources.recordDescription: One Connecticut town that counts as a distressed municipality for environmental justice purposes in 2025, and whether it is in an eligibility grace period.
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29: New Haven (TOWN_NO 93) is listed with GRACE_PERIOD Yes.

sources.title: USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset: 12-digit subwatersheds
sources.recordDescription: One 12-digit hydrologic unit (subwatershed) with its name, area and the unit it drains into.

sources.title: National Weather Service: forecast for a point
sources.recordDescription: The forecast office and grid for one point, with links to its 12-hour and hourly forecasts.

queryNotes.allRecords: Two steps: /points/{lat},{lon} gives properties.forecast and properties.forecastHourly; fetch those for the periods.
queryNotes.clients: Send a User-Agent naming your app and a contact, as the NWS API documentation asks.

sources.title: EPA ATTAINS assessment units (areas: estuaries, lakes, bays)
sources.recordDescription: One estuary, lake or bay segment a state assessed for its water quality report, with use support, impairment causes and listing status.
sources.cost: No key for the map service (observed 2026-10-29).
sources.readinessNote: Tidal rivers and the harbor are here, not in the lines layer: the lower Mill River is CT-C1_023-SB (Not Supporting, category 5, 2024). Rows repeat; de-duplicate by assessmentunitidentifier and reportingcycle.

sources.title: Connecticut tree canopy by census tract (CIRCA)
sources.publisher: UConn Connecticut Institute for Resilience and Climate Adaptation (CIRCA)
sources.recordDescription: One 2020 census tract in Connecticut with the share of its area under tree canopy and its statewide percentile and rank.
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29: CanopyPerc is a fraction (0.056 = 5.6%), not a percent; tract 1424 in Fair Haven is 0.056. GEOID20 uses the 2020 county code (09009), like census-tracts-2020, not the 2022 planning-region codes in the CT DEEP EJ layers. What Percentile and Rank rank is not documented on the layer.

sources.title: CT DEEP combined sewer overflow (CSO) outfall locations
sources.publisher: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection
sources.recordDescription: One combined sewer overflow outfall, or group of outfalls, with the sewer authority and the water it discharges to.
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29: 57 locations, including a Greater New Haven outfall to the Mill River at Mitchell Drive. These are where overflows happen, not when: it is not an alert feed, so pair it with rainfall before a river workday.

sources.title: National Weather Service: station observations
sources.recordDescription: One observation at a weather station (temperature, wind, precipitation over the last hours) at one time.
sources.readinessNote: Checked 2026-10-29 at KHVN (Tweed-New Haven): precipitation fields are often null or absent, so 'no rain reported' is not 'no rain'. Use /observations?limit=… for recent history.

queryNotes.clients: Send a User-Agent naming your app and a contact.

fields.conversion: iNaturalist observation id; the public page is https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/{id}
observed_on when there is no time
true → planted or cultivated; otherwise unknown unless taxon.introduced/native (with a place_id)
strip <i> tags; the authorship follows the name
USDA region codes (L48 lower 48, CAN, AK, HI, PR...), not states
true → potentially-invasive, false → invasive; region is US-CT
Yes → prohibited (CGS 22a-381d), with any effective date given
the list's name; match other authorities via synonyms
percent below 200% of the federal poverty level
